title: How Much Does It Cost to Carpet Stairs in Seattle?
meta: Carpeting stairs in Seattle is priced per step, and tread count, wrap method, fiber and pad drive the total. Wills Flooring explains what changes your quote.
keywords: cost to carpet stairs Seattle, carpet stairs price per step, how much to carpet a staircase, stair carpet installation Seattle WA, waterfall vs Hollywood stair carpet cost

blocks.lead: Stair carpet in Seattle is priced per step, not per square foot, and the total depends on how many treads you have, how they are shaped, how the carpet is wrapped, and which fiber and pad you choose.
blocks.detail: A straight 13-step staircase is a half-day job. Pie-shaped turns, open sides, landings and a thick patterned carpet each add labor and waste. Wills Flooring prices stairs on site after counting and measuring every tread; we do not publish a flat carpet rate.

blocks.html: Seattle is a staircase city. Wallingford and Ballard split-levels have a short run up and a short run down, Queen Anne and Capitol Hill houses have steep, narrow flights with a turn, and every townhome from Beacon Hill to Magnolia has three floors of stairs. So the question comes up constantly, and the honest answer is that stairs are quoted differently from rooms. Here is what goes into the number, how to count your own steps, and where the money actually goes.

blocks.text: Why stairs are priced per step instead of per square foot

items.title: Every step is cut and fitted by hand
items.text: A bedroom is one big piece stretched to the walls. A staircase is thirteen or more small pieces, each cut, padded, stapled at the crotch of the riser and trimmed to the stringer or the wall. Labor per square foot is several times a flat room, which is why the industry counts steps.

items.title: Waste is high
items.text: Carpet comes 12 ft wide. A 3 ft stair uses strips cut from that roll, and patterns have to be matched on every step. A staircase can eat a surprising amount of carpet compared to its footprint, and that waste shows up in your material line.

items.title: Shape changes everything
items.text: A pie-shaped winder tread takes twice as long as a straight one. An open-sided stair with a banister means wrapping the nosing around the end of each tread and finishing the edge cleanly. Bullnose bottom steps and curved landings are the most labor of all.

items.title: Old Seattle stairs are rarely square
items.text: Craftsman and Tudor staircases have settled for a century. Treads are out of level, risers vary in height, and nosings are worn round. Good installers pad and stretch to hide it. Fast installers leave puckers you see every time you climb.

blocks.text: The five things that move a Seattle stair carpet quote

head: Factor
Adds cost when
Why
rows: More than 13 steps, or any landing
Each step is a unit of labor. A landing is measured as a small room and seamed to the steps above and below.
Each pie step is patterned, cut and matched individually. Three winders often cost as much as six straight steps.
The carpet wraps under the nosing and the edge is finished by hand. Two open sides doubles that work.
Hollywood (cap and band) instead of waterfall
Hollywood tucks the carpet tight under each nosing for a tailored look. It takes longer and uses more staples and pad than a simple waterfall drape.
Wool, patterned or thick pile; premium pad
Material is the biggest swing in any carpet quote. Patterns need matching on every step, and dense pad is trimmed and fitted per tread.
Old carpet, tack strip and hundreds of staples
Pulling stair carpet is slow. Every staple has to come out before new pad goes down, especially if the treads underneath are hardwood you may want later.

blocks.text: Waterfall vs Hollywood: the look and the labor

a.title: Choose waterfall when
items: You want the lower labor cost and a softer, more casual look
The carpet is a Berber or loop that does not bend crisply
Nosings are worn round on an older Seattle staircase
The stairs are enclosed on both sides

b.title: Choose Hollywood when
items: You want the tailored, upholstered look buyers expect in Queen Anne or Magnolia
The carpet is a cut pile or a pattern that shows the nosing line
One or both sides are open with a banister
You are pairing carpet stairs with hardwood floors above and below

blocks.text: How stair carpet compares to hardwood or vinyl plank on stairs

blocks.html: Since we do publish rates for hard-surface stairs, they make a useful reference point. Wills Flooring installs hardwood on stairs at $125 per stair and vinyl plank or laminate on stairs at $100 per stair, labor only, with material quoted separately. A 13-step staircase is $1,625 in hardwood labor or $1,300 in vinyl plank labor before material. Carpet stairs land below those labor numbers in most cases, but the material choice can move the total in either direction, which is exactly why we price carpet on site.

blocks.title: Seattle condo and townhome note:
blocks.text: Many Capitol Hill and Belltown buildings require carpet on stairs and upper floors for sound. If your HOA has an acoustic rule, ask for the required pad rating before you shop. We bring the spec sheet so the building manager can sign off, and we handle the elevator reservation and parking permit for the install day.
What a Seattle stair install day looks like

items.text: Old carpet, pad, tack strip and staples come out. On 1920s to 1950s houses we check whether the treads are finished fir or oak you might want to refinish instead.

items.d: Pad and tack strip, about 1 hour
items.text: New pad is cut and stapled per tread with a gap at the nosing. Tack strip goes at the crotch of each riser for a stretch-in stair.
Each step is stretched with a knee kicker, stapled, and trimmed. Hollywood wraps add time. Pie treads and open sides add more.
Landings are seamed last so the pattern runs true. You can walk on the stairs immediately.
items.note: A straight run is done by early afternoon; a turned, open staircase is a full day.

blocks.text: How to get an honest stair carpet quote in Seattle

items.html: Count your treads before anyone visits. Include landings and note which steps are pie-shaped or open on a side. That count is the backbone of every honest quote.
Ask for the wrap method on the quote. Waterfall and Hollywood should be named, because they are different amounts of work and look different.
Pick a stair-rated carpet. Dense low pile, nylon or triexta, holds up to the concentrated wear on stair nosings far better than a soft plush. Our best carpet for stairs post explains why.
Ask what is under the old carpet. Many Ballard and Wallingford stairs hide finished fir treads. Refinishing them at $55 to $75 per tread is sometimes the better call than new carpet.

Insist on a firm written number. Wills Flooring measures every step, brings the samples, and writes the price on the spot, backed by a 1-year workmanship warranty. See what the carpet installation visit includes.

faq.q: How is carpet for stairs priced?
faq.a: By the step, plus material. Installers count the treads, note any landings, pie-shaped turns and open sides, then add the carpet and pad needed including waste. Wills Flooring gives a firm written total after measuring every step at the free estimate rather than publishing a flat per-step rate.

faq.q: How much carpet do I need for 13 stairs?
faq.a: A typical closed stair with 3 ft wide treads uses roughly 18 to 20 inches of carpet per step, so 13 steps need about 20 to 22 linear feet cut from a 12 ft roll, which yields several strips. Pie treads, open sides and pattern matching add to that. We measure and calculate it for you.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to carpet stairs or install hardwood on them?
faq.a: In labor, carpet is usually less. Wills Flooring installs hardwood on stairs at $125 per stair and vinyl plank at $100 per stair, so a 13-step flight is $1,625 or $1,300 in labor before material. Carpet stair labor typically comes in under those, though a premium wool can change the total.

faq.q: What is the difference between waterfall and Hollywood stair carpet?
faq.a: Waterfall drapes the carpet over each nosing and straight down the riser in one flow, which is faster and suits loops and Berbers. Hollywood, also called cap and band, wraps the carpet tightly under the nosing for a tailored, upholstered edge. Hollywood takes longer and costs more in labor.

faq.q: How long does it take to carpet a staircase?
faq.a: A straight 13-step staircase takes about half a day including tear-out. A staircase with a turn, pie-shaped treads, open sides or a landing can take a full day. You can use the stairs as soon as the installer finishes; there is no cure time with stretch-in carpet.

faq.q: Do Seattle condos require carpet on stairs?
faq.a: Many do. Multi-level condos and townhomes in Capitol Hill, Belltown and Queen Anne often have HOA acoustic rules requiring carpet and a rated pad on stairs and upper floors. Ask for the required pad rating before choosing, and we will bring the specification sheet for the building to approve.
